statistic: RUWE — the renormalised unit weight error of a Gaia astrometric solution
deriving_document: Lindegren (2018), GAIA-C3-TN-LU-LL-124-01, §6 ‘An example using the RUWE’ — where 1.4 is read off a histogram of 338 833 sources nominally within 100 pc, cut at parallax significance > 10; the note's Conclusions do not contain the number
provenance_note: Transcribed from circulation-measure-ruwe.py (tick 21, 2026-08-01), whose result is landed in circulation-measure-ruwe.csv. Nothing here is new: the profile is the same instrument written down where it can be replaced. The comment in that script about the two Lindegren documents being one character apart in most bibliographies is the reason `cite_lindegren` and `cite_tn` are separate flags, and the reason every load-bearing hit is hand-read.

cite_lindegren.note: any Lindegren citation in the window — NOT evidence that the technical note is meant

cite_tn.note: the deriving document identified as such

prov.note: the sample or the reading the number came from

repair_0_5: F2 (2026-08-09): the term's boundaries were \b, which fails against an underscore because _ is a word character — a subscripted identifier such as ruwe_2<1.4 was not a term match and its stated threshold was invisible. The boundaries are now (?<![A-Za-z0-9]) and (?![A-Za-z]), so a subscript or an index digit is admitted and an embedding letter still is not. F1: the site patterns take the engine's {GAP}, whose period rule lets a site cross an intervening decimal number.
repair_0_6: tick 55, 2026-08-10. P-A: the site patterns take the engine's {VGAP} — the step from the relation to its number, which under 0.5 was \s* and therefore failed on 'greater than THE 1.4 level' (G6, 2111.03887) and on a table row whose cells read 'RUWE & < & 5' (G4, 2405.13395). {VGAP} admits whitespace, table-cell separators and at most one article. P-B: the long form of the term admits one optional letter — re-?nor?mali[sz]ed — because 2112.07023 writes 'renomalised unit weight error' at the site of its threshold and the sieve's English was correct where the paper's was not. The three following words make a false positive on that letter essentially impossible. Applied to BOTH Gaia profiles: they read one corpus and are declared to share one invoking set (tick 47 §0.1), so a spelling admitted in one and not the other would silently split that set. Registered as an amendment in ../PREREGISTRATION-tick55.md §1, before any measurement of this tick.
